issue_request: FHIR-28594 was Published/Not Persuasive with Modification for R5 SubscriptionTopic. The Jira asked to change SubscriptionTopic.resourceTrigger.resourceType away from a fixed resource-type value set to a URI representation that can name different FHIR versions and custom resources, remove targetProfile-oriented wording, and link to ElementDefinition.type.code.
initial_application: The first-pass commit 4f3fcec0394 changed the historical resourceTrigger.resourceType selector from a code/token-shaped resource-type selector to uri with an extensible FHIR-defined-type binding. The Jira-cited 70355f13b223 commit was part of the same SubscriptionTopic implementation package but mostly adjusted maturity/status and documentation. Follow-up commit dbeb5e6a7aa removed the stale targetProfile definition wording and added the ElementDefinition.type.code link, and the 2021 source rework carried that wording into structuredefinition-SubscriptionTopic.xml.
additional_context: Later applied and published SubscriptionTopic work renamed resourceTrigger.resourceType to resourceTrigger.resource, clarified adjacent resource-selector definitions, changed the binding family to SubscriptionTypes/version-independent resource types, and collapsed resourceTrigger/eventTrigger into the current trigger backbone with fhir.ini aliases for old R5 paths. The tightly related later issues FHIR-38800, FHIR-39024, FHIR-33973, and FHIR-46492 are already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. Current source/subscriptiontopic/structuredefinition-SubscriptionTopic.xml defines SubscriptionTopic.trigger.resource as uri, explains relative URLs against the StructureDefinition root with the Patient example, links to ElementDefinition.type.code, and no longer uses targetProfiles for this selector. The current extensible ValueSet/subscription-types binding reflects later accepted subscription-selector decisions rather than an unfinished FHIR-28594 application.
